decisions.reason: The button configuration is an independent decision in another clause of message 887 and is already represented by its own same-message Events; the VRTC/VBACKUP change does not alter it.
The PIR and touch biasing statement is an independent clause already represented by its own same-message Event; the VRTC/VBACKUP decision does not change that requirement.
The instruction to leave the VBACKUP pad unpopulated applies only to the AXP2101 backup-power provision and does not change the display-backlight circuit or its population choices.
Leaving VRTC unconnected and exposing VBACKUP does not alter the placement or identity of the AXP2101 and MT3608 decoupling capacitors.
The source retains the existing AXP2101 and specifies auxiliary-pin handling; it does not change the selected power-management component, required rails, charging behavior, or efficiency goal.
The AXP2101 VRTC/VBACKUP decision is unrelated to the existing ESP32 decoupling configuration.

Locating a small VBACKUP pad or via beside PWROK is fully captured by the auxiliary-pin requirement and does not necessarily change any current board-orientation, connector-access, enclosure, or antenna-layout constraint.
The VRTC and VBACKUP handling does not alter the required current-measurement capability or the conditional omission of a separate INA device.
This candidate concerns the separate power board's VMID/VSYS topology and thermal pad; the integrated-board VRTC/VBACKUP decision does not change those requirements.
The AXP2101 auxiliary-pin change does not affect the quantity, type, interface, or purpose of the display light-sensor connector.
Exposing an unpopulated VBACKUP pad is a specific electrical-design choice and does not modify the existing cost, sourcing, connector-reduction, or functionality-preservation rules.
The VRTC/VBACKUP details operate within the already selected integrated-board architecture and do not change its consolidation or functionality-preservation state.
